source: Minchat Shai on Lev 4:34 (Zevachim 37b-38a; Rashi; the Ramah; the Meiri; Shemen Sasson; Ramban responsum 232)
claim_en: The horn-word dispute: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel both read the three outer-altar sin-offering passages (the ruler 4:25, the she-goat 4:30, the lamb 4:34) on the premise that ONE of them writes qarnot ('horns') FULL. MS rules: 'ALL the books and their Masorah lists agree — all three are LEAN, not one full... and wherever the Talmud disputes the Masorah on lean-and-full we follow the Masorah, even where law hangs on it.' SNAPSHOT sides with the Masorah: every qarnot of the chapter's dispute-stations lean — five lean tokens in the Torah, the three of the dispute among them.

source: Minchat Shai on Lev 4:34 (the Masorah's complement)
claim_en: The FULL horn-form's own four stations: the golden inner altar of the anointed priest's bull (4:7) first, then the altar-purgings of the investiture, the eighth day, and Yom Kippur.

im ('if', opening the anointed priest's case): MS rules 'with GALGAL (the wheel-accent), not with maqqef' — the unjoined half stands in-stream (no joining stroke); SNAPSHOT writes the munach (the upright conjunctive stroke) where MS's books write the wheel: galgal-class station 5.
techeta / yecheta ('shall sin'): 'the chet with hataf segol (the compound half-vowel)' — BOTH stations, the sin-verb's guttural carrying the three-dot compound mark, in-stream.

source: Minchat Shai on Lev 4:4 (the sevirin list)
claim_en: 'He shall bring the bull to the door of the tent of meeting BEFORE the LORD' — the scribes' conjecture (sevirin) expects asher lifne ('WHICH is before the LORD'); the verse writes no asher at all. The rejected-conjecture class; the list's partner is Solomon's bronze altar (2 Chr 1:5-6, outside the Torah instrument).

'And the priest shall dip HIS FINGER' — some err and recite et here, says MS: the FIRST passage (4:6) writes 'et his-finger', this one writes the finger WITHOUT et. Verified structurally: this is the ONLY place in the Torah where ha-kohen ('the priest') is directly followed by etzbao ('his finger').

source: Minchat Shai on Lev 4:18 quoting the Ramah
claim_en: yesod ('the base' of the altar): 'every yesod in the Torah is written FULL with vav' — the Ramah's rule verified WHOLE: nine stations, all full, zero lean forms in the stream.

source: Minchat Shai + Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Lev 4:31 (the Masorah)
claim_en: husar ('was removed', of the fat): the Masorah pair — 'as the fat IS REMOVED' here, 'from the time the daily offering WAS REMOVED' (Dan 12:11, outside the instrument) — the Kitzur: when the daily offering was removed, removed too was the fat whose merit fed blessing into everything. In the Torah the word stands ONCE, written full; MS records books split on its stress (fore-stressed vs end-stressed), a variance filed named.

The lamb-passage's pointing pair: ha-chatat ('the sin-offering', 4:33) — 'the tet DAGESHED (the hardening dot)', in-stream; and temima ('unblemished', 4:32) — 'the tav SOFT', asserted at build (no dot in the stream).
mi-zevach ha-shelamim ('from the SACRIFICE of the peace-offerings'): 'the zayin DAGESHED' — the doubling dot after the assimilated min, in-stream.
